mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals a loosening of monetary policy, which typically leads to increased liquidity in the market and thus higher S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of the instances where FEDFUNDS decreases by > 0.25%.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) indicates a strengthening labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and spending, leading to higher S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of the instances where PAYEMS increases.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) suggests increased consumer demand, which can lead to higher corporate earnings and thus positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where RSAFS increases by > 1%.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) signals a strengthening supply side of the economy, which can lead to higher corporate profits and thus positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of the instances where INDPRO increases by > 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates a tightening labor market, which can lead to wage inflation and increased consumer spending, driving up S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of the instances where UNRATE decreases by > 0.2%.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 5% and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) is rising, it indicates inflationary pressure and tightening monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 5% and CPIAUCSL increases by > 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where FEDFUNDS > 5% and CPIAUCSL increases by > 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) and real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) both increase, it signals a strong demand side of the economy, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS both increase by > 1% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of the instances where both HOUST and RSAFS increase by > 1%.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) coupled with an increase in unemployment rate (UNRATE) suggests a weakening economy, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO decreases by > 0.5% and UNRATE increases by > 0.2% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where INDPRO decreases by > 0.5% and UNRATE increases by > 0.2%.
